rulings.challenge_claim: The header-class contrast is byte-false as a discriminator: the seeing-verb clause the row treats as distinctive to this header is byte-identical in both superscriptions, leaving only the head noun to carry the distinction; and the companion header decision states the shared fact correctly, so two accounts of the same bytes disagree inside one cluster.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, not from the challenge. The relative clause is אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.1.1 (tokens 5-6 of 16) and אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.2.1 (tokens 2-3 of 9); collated in both directions the run returns BYTE tier, so the seeing-verb is shared, not distinctive. The row's device_notes nevertheless read 'The header uses the seeing-verb chazah rather than the word-formula of the 2:1 header' - the 'rather than' sets the seeing-verb against the second header, which its own bytes carry. The only byte-true discriminator is the head noun: חֲזוֹן֙ at oshb:Isa.1.1 token 1 against הַדָּבָר֙ at oshb:Isa.2.1 token 1; the row's second clause ('differ in header-noun class') states this correctly, so the defect is confined to the first clause's framing. The intra-cluster contradiction is confirmed: the P01-008 device_notes say 'both retain the chazah seeing-verb and the ben-Amots patronymic', which the bytes support and which contradicts P01-001 as written. Row-internal checks that hold: oshb:Isa.1.1 is 16 tokens carrying a header noun, a relative clause and a four-king regnal list with no imperative, vocative or divine-speech frame, so the single-verse isolation ground stands; no parashah mark falls in the span and none is claimed; no ketiv/qere note falls in chapter 1 (verified against the 49-verse single-witness inventory); identity numbering, no offset zone touched, no dual owed. The challenge's ancillary observation is byte-true and independently re-derived: oshb:Isa.1.1 token 14 is יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ, the yod-initial regnal byform, returned by a token-exact skeleton sweep at exactly 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse), against 28 verses for the token-exact yod-less spelling and 30 verses for its substring form. Staged book guidance calls the yod-initial byform unattested in Isaiah; the bytes of this verse contradict that. This is a staged-guidance erratum, NOT a row defect - the row makes no spelling claim - and it carries no remedy against the row.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-001 device_notes, first clause. Change: replace the 'seeing-verb chazah rather than the word-formula of the 2:1 header' contrast with a statement that both superscriptions carry the same relative clause (byte tier at oshb:Isa.1.1 and oshb:Isa.2.1) and that the header-noun class is the sole discriminator (חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙, byte tier). Test the cure must pass: a byte collate of the relative-clause run against oshb:Isa.2.1 returns byte tier - the test that killed the original - and the corrected sentence must read consistently with the P01-008 account of the same clause. Splice both runs from source; do not re-key. No boundary change is proposed or implied.

rulings.challenge_claim: The load-bearing ground for this cut - that the summons couplet names no offense yet - is contradicted by the bytes of the row's own first verse, and a catchword straddling its closing seam is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both halves re-derive from bytes. First: oshb:Isa.1.2 is 13 tokens and closes וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי (tokens 11-13, byte tier) - the rebellion charge stands inside the row's own first verse. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative asserts flatly that 'verses 2-3 name no offense yet'; that is byte-false and it is the load-bearing rejection ground. The boundary_rationale's 'before any content of the charge is stated' is defensible only as a within-verse position claim about the summons (שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ, tokens 1-4, byte tier), a reading the row never states, and oshb:Isa.1.3 adds a further indictment of non-recognition, so the couplet as a whole does carry charge content. Second: בָּנִים֙ at oshb:Isa.1.2 token 8 and בָּנִ֖ים at oshb:Isa.1.4 token 9 collate at ACCENT_STRIPPED tier - a catchword in immediately adjacent verses straddling this row's own closing seam (1:3|1:4), undisclosed, and the campaign's cross-seam cohesion rule makes disclosure owed whatever the seam's fate. Object correction to the challenge, which does not disturb the finding: the challenge names the swept object as 'bare plural noun' but reports 14 verses. The bare-token object returns 8 verses (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact); 14 is the substring object, which also collects prefixed and articled forms. The digit is right for the substring object, wrong for the object named. The challenge's rebellion-root digit verifies as stated (sweep: 18 verses, skeleton, substring). The lawsuit-vocabulary contrast the row draws outside its span also verifies at oshb:Isa.3.13. The seam itself survives on the verse-initial woe-lexeme at oshb:Isa.1.4 (byte tier), which is why the defect is a warrant defect rather than a bounds defect. Identity numbering; no mark and no ketiv/qere note in the span.
rulings.remedy: Two fields, one edit each. (1) P01-002 strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'verses 2-3 name no offense yet' with a byte-true ground - the couplet opens with the witness-summons imperatives at tokens 1-4 and the charge follows inside the same verse, so the unit is a summons-plus-indictment preface, not an offense-free preface. (2) P01-002 device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure that the plural-noun catchword recurs at oshb:Isa.1.4 at accent_stripped tier, tier-labelled, with the swept object named (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact). Test the cure must pass: the rewritten rejection ground must survive a byte read of oshb:Isa.1.2 tokens 11-13 - the test that killed the original - and any digit shipped with the catchword disclosure must match the object it names under a token-exact sweep, not a substring sweep. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: A catchword pair crosses this row's closing seam undisclosed while the decision on the far side of that same seam argues its opening from the very same device - an asymmetric disclosure across one shared seam; and the row's 'remnant note' label at 1:9 rides on the English.
rulings.grounds: The device is byte-true and independently re-derived: oshb:Isa.1.9 closes כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ (tokens 8-11, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.1.10 carries קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם (tokens 4-5) and עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה (tokens 9-10), byte tier at each site. The two place-name skeletons stand at 4 and 3 verses book-wide respectively (sweep: 4 verses / 3 verses, skeleton) and fall in adjacent verses only here; the asymmetry is real, since P01-004 argues its own opening from this same repetition while P01-003 does not disclose it. What is wrong is the severity, not the fact. This is a pure symmetry-completion gap, not a warrant defect: the seam is independently carried by the tier-1 imperative-vocative onset at oshb:Isa.1.10 (verified: 10 tokens, verse-initial imperative plus two vocatives) and corroborated at tier-3 by the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.9 (single-witness, correctly typed, and the only marked verse inside 1:4-1:9 - span-relevant mark symmetry complete). The device also functions as a hinge across the seam (simile at 1:9, vocative address at 1:10), so it does not argue continuity in the way an undisclosed cohesion signal ordinarily does; and the cluster is not blind to it, since the paired decision states it. Corrected finding: an owed cross-seam disclosure at low severity, to be completed as a sweep across both rows on the shared seam rather than as a spot fix on one. The secondary point verifies and is smaller still: oshb:Isa.1.9 reads שָׂרִ֖יד (token 6) under the verb הוֹתִ֥יר (token 4) - neither belongs to the four-way remnant family - so 'remnant note' is a translation-carried label; the row's signal keys correctly claim no remnant family, so nothing propagates into the evidence layer. Row-internal checks that hold: the woe lexeme is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.1.4 (byte tier) and the opening-indictment role reading matches the byte role-split; the divine title at oshb:Isa.1.4 is a genuine site of the book's signature title (sweep: 24 verses at the plene spelling, skeleton, plus the defective site at oshb:Isa.49.7 = 25). Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-003 device_notes. Change: add one tier-labelled cross-seam disclosure naming the place-name repetition at oshb:Isa.1.9 and oshb:Isa.1.10 (byte tier at each site; sweep: 4 verses / 3 verses, skeleton, adjacent-verse co-occurrence only here) and stating that it is read as a hinge rather than as continuity. Separately, re-cut the 'remnant note' wording in boundary_rationale so the label follows the Hebrew (a survivor noun, not the remnant family). Test the cure must pass: the disclosure sweep must be run across BOTH rows on this seam, so that no member of the pair is disclosed on one side of a seam and silent on the other - the asymmetry that killed the original; and the re-cut label must not introduce any remnant-family signal key that the bytes do not carry. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: A two-site, book-wide word pair carrying its two governing verbs in inverted order straddles this row's closing seam undisclosed, arguing an address running unbroken past the cut.
rulings.grounds: The lexical fact verifies exactly, digits and objects both. oshb:Isa.1.17 closes שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה (tokens 7-10, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.1.23 carries יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה (tokens 10-14, byte tier): the same two nouns with their governing verbs in inverted order. Token-exact skeleton sweeps return the orphan noun at exactly 2 verses (oshb:Isa.1.17, oshb:Isa.1.23) and the widow noun at exactly 3 (those two plus oshb:Isa.47.8); across the two sites the orphan token matches at accent_stripped tier and the widow token at skeleton tier - all as the challenge states. The framing is wrong. This row's closing seam is 1:17|1:18. The second member of the pair sits at oshb:Isa.1.23 - six verses downstream, beyond the whole of the 1:18-1:20 unit and inside the span of the 1:21-1:26 decision. A recurrence that skips an intervening unit cannot argue continuity ACROSS the 1:17|1:18 seam; nothing in the bytes links oshb:Isa.1.17 to oshb:Isa.1.18. The device is a chapter-level lexical bracket, a different object from adjacent-seam cohesion, and the challenge's conclusion that it argues 'a larger bracket reaching past MT 1:17 against this cut' is not carried by the bytes it cites. Corrected finding: a genuine and notable two-verse book-wide pair goes undisclosed and is owed a chapter-level device note - and it is owed by BOTH rows, since oshb:Isa.1.23 lies inside the 1:21-1:26 span, not only by this one. It is not a cross-seam cohesion signal against this row's cut, and it does not reduce the warrant, so low. Row-internal checks that hold, and one that is exemplary: the onset שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.1.10 (byte tier) and the addressee shift is byte-carried by the two vocatives rather than inferred; the row's own recurrence handling is correct - the summons verb of oshb:Isa.1.2 matches oshb:Isa.1.10 at accent_stripped tier only, and the row explicitly refuses a byte-identical claim and labels the contrast as a byte-checkable form-class observation, which is exactly the tier discipline the campaign requires. The SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.17 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse inside 1:10-1:17. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
rulings.remedy: Field: device_notes, on BOTH rows sharing the device - P01-004 (which holds oshb:Isa.1.17) and P01-006 (which holds oshb:Isa.1.23). Change: add one tier-labelled sentence naming the orphan/widow pair with its inverted verb order, per-site tiers (orphan accent_stripped, widow skeleton across the two sites), and the swept object and digits (sweep: 2 verses / 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact), explicitly classed as a chapter-level lexical bracket and NOT as cross-seam cohesion at 1:17|1:18. Test the cure must pass: the disclosure must not be phrased as evidence bearing on the 1:17|1:18 seam - the framing error that killed the original challenge - and the digit shipped must match a token-exact sweep of the object named. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The frame-ownership ground for this seam is carried by the English rendering alone, sits nowhere near the seam in the bytes, and recurs mid-verse inside the block immediately upstream that the row contrasts itself against; and the closing formula is called a recognized oracle-closing signature with neither tier label nor digit, that skeleton standing at 3 verses of which only 1:20 carries the ki-form.
rulings.grounds: The load-bearing half is upheld and re-derives exactly. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative rejects attaching 1:18-1:20 to the preceding unit because 'verse 18 opens a new speech-act explicitly framed by its own says-Yahweh signature' - but no Hebrew is quoted for that frame anywhere in the row, and in the bytes the form is יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Isa.1.18 tokens 4-5 of 16, not at the seam and framing nothing there. The same quotative stands mid-verse at oshb:Isa.1.11 as יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, tokens 5-6 of 17, INSIDE the block the row contrasts itself against; the two collate at accent_stripped tier. Naming the object before the digit and re-deriving it independently: the bare imperfect quotative adjacent to the tetragrammaton is attested at exactly 5 verses (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton - oshb:Isa.1.11, oshb:Isa.1.18, oshb:Isa.33.10, oshb:Isa.41.21, oshb:Isa.66.9) and must not be blended with the 5 vav-prefixed narrative-onset sites (oshb:Isa.3.16, oshb:Isa.7.3, oshb:Isa.8.1, oshb:Isa.8.3, oshb:Isa.20.3). On that object the form cannot discriminate an onset from a mid-unit interjection, so the stated rejection ground does not carry the seam, and the engagement gap is real. The second half of the challenge is byte-FALSE and must be corrected. The four-token closing run כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר at oshb:Isa.1.20 (tokens 6-9) collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.40.5, where it stands as כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (tokens 8-11), and against oshb:Isa.58.14, where it stands as כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (tokens 13-16); a skeleton sweep on the four-token run returns exactly those 3 verses. All three sites carry the ki-form, byte-identically down to the accents - so 'only MT 1:20 carries the ki-form' is contradicted by the bytes the challenge itself cites. The corrected reading makes the row's 'recognized oracle-closing signature' description stronger than the challenge allowed: a byte-identical four-token formula at 3 verses book-wide. The row's defect on that half therefore reduces to the tier-and-digit omission, which is real under the campaign's tier-disclosure law but is a labelling gap, not a false claim. Severity stays medium because the upheld half is the row's rejection warrant. What holds: the onset לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.1.18 (tokens 1-3, byte tier) and carries the seam on its own; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.20 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse in the span; identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
rulings.remedy: Two fields. (1) P01-005 strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the rejection so it rests on the verse-initial imperative-plus-cohortative onset לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.18, tokens 1-3, byte tier), and either drop the quotative as a discriminator or splice it and disclose that it stands at tokens 4-5 and recurs mid-verse at oshb:Isa.1.11 inside the contrasted block (accent_stripped tier across the two sites; sweep: 5 verses, skeleton, bare quotative, not blended with the 5 vav-prefixed narrative sites). (2) P01-005 boundary_rationale: tier-label and digit the closing formula - byte tier, 3 verses (oshb:Isa.1.20, oshb:Isa.40.5, oshb:Isa.58.14), all three carrying the ki-form. Tests the cure must pass: a collate of the quotative run against oshb:Isa.1.11 returns accent_stripped - the test that killed the original discriminator; and a collate of the four-token closing run against oshb:Isa.40.5 and oshb:Isa.58.14 returns byte at both - the test that killed the challenge's 'only 1:20' sub-claim, so the corrected digit must not be written as 1. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The decision and every tier label verify exactly as written, but the one ground offered against the rival division - that the divine-speech signature at MT 1:24 is postpositive and not an onset - is contested by that form's byte position.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the bytes. oshb:Isa.1.24 is 12 tokens: לָכֵ֗ן at token 1, נְאֻ֤ם at token 2, and the quoted divine speech ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי running from token 8 to token 12. The signature therefore stands after nothing but a discourse connective and AHEAD of the speech it introduces: at this site it heads the speech rather than following it. Independently re-derived census: the signature stands in 23 verses (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton, token-exact and substring agreeing) and is verse-initial at exactly one, oshb:Isa.56.8; every other site sits at token 3 or later, so oshb:Isa.1.24 is the earliest position in the book bar one. The campaign's tier-disclosure law makes form-class and position labels byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits, and 'postpositive ... not an onset frame in itself' is used here as a load-bearing ground for rejecting the 1:23|1:24 rival. On the bytes of this verse that ground does not hold, and it leans toward the rival that the tier-3 mark also points to. Upheld. Calibration - the row is otherwise exact and the cut is not defeated, which fixes severity at low. Independently confirmed: קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה at oshb:Isa.1.21 (tokens 4-5) and קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה at oshb:Isa.1.26 (tokens 12-13) collate at SKELETON tier in both directions and no higher, exactly matching the row's own skeleton-tier labelling and its two-verse digit; the woe lexeme at oshb:Isa.1.24 is genuinely non-initial (token 8) and governs first-person divine action, so the self-exclamation role reading holds; the PE at oshb:Isa.1.23 is correctly typed, never conflated with the chapter's SAMEKH sites, is the only marked verse inside 1:21-1:26, and is disclosed as the rival rather than buried, with confidence honestly reduced to medium_low. The challenge's 'available and unused' observation also verifies: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה at oshb:Isa.1.25 token 1 collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.1.26, whose token 1 is וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה - a byte-tier anaphora, but lying wholly on the far side of the rival cut, so it does not answer it. Not escalated: the strategy settles the precedence in play (a byte-grounded cohesion device outranks a tier-3 single-witness mark, and tier-3 never drives), and the residual 21-26 versus 21-23|24-26 question is a boundary matter the row already discloses and holds at reduced confidence - a proposal for boss adoption, not a peer policy escalation. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-006 device_notes (and the matching clause in strongest_rejected_alternative). Change: drop the unqualified 'postpositive ... not an onset frame in itself' at this site, or qualify it to the bytes - the signature stands at token 2 of 12, after the connective and ahead of the quoted speech, and across the 23-verse census it is verse-initial only at oshb:Isa.56.8 - and rest the rejection of the 1:23|1:24 rival on the skeleton-tier bracket alone, which the row already labels honestly. Test the cure must pass: any retained position label must survive a token-index read of oshb:Isa.1.24 placing the signature at token 2 of 12 ahead of the speech - the test that killed the original - and no digit may be shipped without naming whether its object is the token-exact signature or a substring. This is a prose and form-label repair only: the span is untouched, and re-opening the 21-26 division would be a boundary proposal requiring explicit boss adoption, never author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row asserts its opening seam carries no explicit lexical frame marker; in the bytes a two-term pair that co-occurs in only two verses of this chapter sits at exactly this row's opening verse and the preceding unit's opening verse. Second and smaller: the pointed splice for the closing verse stops short of the English paired with it.
rulings.grounds: The digits verify and one object label does not. Independently re-derived: the justice noun's substring sweep returns 40 verses; the justice/righteousness co-occurrence object returns 16 verses book-wide and exactly 2 inside chapter 1, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27 (sweep: 16 verses / 2 verses, skeleton) - the challenge's digits are exact. Object correction: the challenge calls it 'the bare justice noun' at oshb:Isa.1.17, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27, but at oshb:Isa.1.27 the form is בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט (token 2), prefixed, not the bare noun מִשְׁפָּ֗ט of oshb:Isa.1.21 (token 7); the accent_stripped match at that site is a substring match, not a token match. The framing is wrong on the first point. The row asserts that the 26|27 seam is 'argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame MARKER'. A frame marker in this book's spine is an onset device - imperative, vocative, messenger or speech formula, superscription, header. A thematic term-pair is a cohesion device, a different object. Verified: oshb:Isa.1.27 is 5 tokens, צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה, carrying no imperative, vocative or speech formula, so the row's assertion is byte-true as written and is not contradicted. What is genuinely defective is an undisclosed cross-seam cohesion signal - and the strongest form of it is not the one the challenge names. The immediately ADJACENT link across the row's own opening seam is the righteousness root: הַצֶּ֔דֶק at oshb:Isa.1.26 token 11 against בִּצְדָקָֽה at oshb:Isa.1.27 token 5, byte tier at each cited site, in consecutive verses, with צֶ֛דֶק at oshb:Isa.1.21 token 8 anchoring the same root at the preceding unit's opening. Adjacent-verse root cohesion across a seam the row itself grades weakest is the disclosure that is owed; the 1:21/1:27 co-occurrence is a chapter-level bracket riding behind it. Severity stays medium: the row states that it has named its sole basis for this seam, and it has not. The second point is upheld exactly as written and is independent. The row's pointed splice for the closing verse is a byte-tier PREFIX of oshb:Isa.1.31 ending at וּבָעֲר֧וּ (token 6 of 10), while the English paired with it in the same field renders the whole verse through the burning and the unquenched fire, which in the Hebrew is שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה (tokens 7-10) and lies outside the quoted run. Quote and gloss are not cut to the same extent, and campaign law repairs that by re-cutting the gloss. What holds: the discourse-mode shift is byte-carried, since oshb:Isa.1.25 and oshb:Isa.1.26 both open with the first-person cohortative וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה and oshb:Isa.1.27 does not; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.31 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse in the span. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
rulings.remedy: Two fields. (1) P01-007 device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure, tier-labelled and per-site, naming the adjacent-verse righteousness-root link oshb:Isa.1.26 to oshb:Isa.1.27 as the primary undisclosed cohesion signal, with the chapter-level term-pair bracket oshb:Isa.1.21 / oshb:Isa.1.27 named second and its object stated correctly (sweep: 16 verses book-wide / 2 verses in the chapter, skeleton, co-occurrence object; the site at oshb:Isa.1.27 is prefixed, not the bare noun). Leave the 'no explicit lexical frame marker' statement standing - it is byte-true and must not be edited away. (2) P01-007 boundary_rationale: re-cut the GLOSS to the extent of the pointed splice, so the English paired with the closing quote ends where the Hebrew ends. Tests the cure must pass: the disclosure must name the adjacent 1:26|1:27 pair, since a bracket claim that skips the intervening verses was what left the real signal invisible; and after the gloss re-cut, quote and gloss must cover the same token range of oshb:Isa.1.31 - the parity test that killed the original. No boundary change is proposed; the 21-31 division question remains the row's own disclosed rival.

rulings.challenge_claim: The shared-feature claim across the two headers ships without tier labels, and its parts sit at three different tiers - one byte-identical, one accent-stripped-only, one skeleton-only.
rulings.grounds: Every tier re-derives exactly as the challenge states, checked in the direction the row's own sentence asserts. The row's device_notes read 'both retain the chazah seeing-verb and the ben-Amots patronymic' - one flat, untiered recurrence claim covering three elements that collate at three different tiers: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.1.1, tokens 5-6) against oshb:Isa.2.1 returns BYTE; the seer's name יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ (oshb:Isa.1.1, token 2) against oshb:Isa.2.1, whose token 4 is יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ, returns ACCENT_STRIPPED; the patronymic בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ (oshb:Isa.1.1, tokens 3-4) against oshb:Isa.2.1, whose tokens 5-6 are בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ, returns SKELETON - the construct form differs in its dagesh and the name in its accent. The campaign's tier-disclosure law requires every recurrence claim to be tier-labelled at write time; this one is not, and it folds a byte-tier element together with an accent-stripped and a skeleton-tier element as though they were one grade of evidence. The strongest half - the byte-identical relative clause - is the half that goes uncited as such, which is also what makes the competing account of the same clause at the other header verse (the P01-001 defect) detectable. Upheld. Severity low is right: the row's bounds and its head-noun contrast are sound and the defect is a labelling failure, not a false claim. Independently confirmed: the onset הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.2.1 (byte tier); the head-noun contrast חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙ is byte-true; oshb:Isa.2.1 is 9 tokens with no imperative, vocative or divine-speech frame, so the single-verse isolation ground holds; the SAMEKH cited upstream at oshb:Isa.1.31 is correctly typed and single-witness; no mark falls inside the one-verse span and the row correctly leaves that absence as no evidence either way. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapters 1-2.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-008 device_notes, the shared-feature sentence. Change: split the untiered claim into per-element tier labels - relative clause byte tier, seer's name accent_stripped tier, patronymic skeleton tier (construct dagesh and name accent both differ) - and cite the byte-tier element as the strongest of the three rather than leaving it unmarked. Test the cure must pass: each element's stated tier must reproduce under a collate of that spliced run against oshb:Isa.2.1 - the test that killed the original flat assertion - and no element may retain a 'verbatim' or 'byte-identical' wording unless its collate actually returns byte. Splice each run from source; do not re-key. No boundary change is proposed.

supported_sample.notes: The inventory records oshb:Isa.2.4 as PE. The type is correct and is not conflated with setumah: chapter 2's other marks are a SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.2.11 and a PE at oshb:Isa.2.22, both outside the span, and no other verse in 2:2-2:4 is marked - so the mark cited is the only one in the span and span-relevant mark symmetry is complete (1 marked verse of the 209 marked verses book-wide). Single-witness disclosure is present in the row, the layer is treated as tier-3, and it is not made the driver: the row pairs it with the verse-5 onset, which also verifies - oshb:Isa.2.5 is 6 tokens opening בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ (byte tier), a vocative followed by a 2mp imperative, a fresh address rather than a continuation. Two byte facts recorded alongside, neither disturbing the verdict. First, a precision slip the row shares with its packet: the quoted eschatological run בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים re-collates at byte tier but stands at tokens 2-3 of 16, since oshb:Isa.2.2 opens with וְהָיָ֣ה at token 1 - so 'Opens with the eschatological formula' overstates position by one token. Second, no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in chapters 1-2 (checked against the 49-verse single-witness inventory), so nothing is owed there, and chapters 2-4 are identity numbering in both witnesses, so no offset-zone dual qualifier is owed anywhere in this cluster.
